codeReview.summary: Feature requirements are largely met: frontend STOMP/SockJS hook is integrated at Layout level, subscribes to /user/topic/budget-alerts, renders global toast notifications with severity styling, and supports auto/manual dismiss with test coverage.

issues.description: The client sends X-User-Id via STOMP connectHeaders, but backend auth for WebSocket is performed during SockJS HTTP handshake (WebSocketAuthInterceptor.beforeHandshake reads HTTP header). This means the configured header may be ignored for user selection; current flow still works with default fake user, but user-scoped alert routing can drift for non-default users.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Shared architecture docs do not capture a key WebSocket auth nuance: STOMP CONNECT headers are distinct from HTTP handshake headers used by current backend auth interceptor.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/useWebSocket.ts:69 sends connectHeaders; backend/src/main/java/com/expensetracker/config/WebSocketAuthInterceptor.java:35 reads servlet handshake header USER_ID_HEADER.

summary: websocket-frontend is functionally implemented and aligns with expected behavior for global alert toasts and subscription flow. I marked one non-blocking integration risk around user identity propagation in WebSocket auth headers and noted two shared-state gaps (skill procedure adherence tracking and missing handshake/header nuance in knowledge docs).
